brief: October was a painful month for global hedge funds, with net returns down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis and performance deteriorating sharply even as US and European indices stayed roughly flat to up, pointing to broad de-risking concentrated in AI and Tech rather than an index-level selloff. Positioning Intelligence does not call the de-risking capitulatory, but flags that prior similarly sharp alpha drawdowns have tended to precede rebounds, that de-grossing (especially among multi-strategy funds) has been widespread, and that Momentum exposure is now only about 30% of its peak, so alpha could rebound even though lingering risks (quant de-grossing, elevated US Tech futures positioning) limit conviction. Separately, JPM is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring the US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) over Europe, and sees US midterm elections as historically supportive for SPX returns over the following 6 to 12 months. On credit, JPM argues AI infrastructure financing is tightening in terms but not facing a broader funding crisis, since hyperscalers remain fundamentally well-positioned while leveraged GPU and data-center developers face more constrained terms. France's fiscal strain is treated as an idiosyncratic story rather than a euro-wide contagion risk.
